This is a beautifully written piece of prose, evoking a sense of place, memory, and the slow passage of time. The description of the lighthouse, the cottage, and the fading maps creates a vivid picture of a place that has been quietly changed by the sea and the passage of years.

The repetition of the opening paragraph serves to emphasize the enduring nature of the lighthouse, even as it is no longer lit. The idea that the tower remains a landmark, a point of reference for sailors, is a powerful concept. The shadow of the tower moving with the tide is a particularly poetic image, suggesting that the tower is part of the water itself.

The description of the keeper's cottage adds to the sense of history. The grey stone, the slate roof, the windows set deep into the walls, and the sloping floors all contribute to the feeling of a place that has been used for generations. The cold stove and the faded tea tin are small details that remind us of the passage of time.

The section about maps and the way they were drawn by hand, with the attention to detail that a satellite image cannot reproduce, is a reminder of the importance of careful measurement and observation.
